mainTopic: רבי יוסי הגלילי and burning a disqualified קרבן; the משנה on burning the bones, sinews, and נותר of the פסח; whether bones that held נותר (שימוש נותר) take on its status
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a קרבן פסח whose owners became טמא or died. רבה adds רבי יוסי הגלילי to the תנאים who burn such a קרבן right away, because he learns that a חטאת whose blood went inside is burned immediately. The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן left him out: a problem in the blood is a problem in the קרבן itself, while the owners are a separate matter. A new משנה then teaches that the bones, sinews, and נותר of the פסח are burned on the 16th of ניסן, and on the 17th if the 16th is שבת. On this משנה, רבי יצחק rules that bones that held נותר (שימוש נותר) make the hands טמא. The גמרא tries to prove his rule from the משנה but rejects the proof: the bones may simply not be broken, following רבי יעקב, who says the ban covers a פסח that was once valid. A ברייתא saying only פסח bones are burned seems to disprove רבי יצחק. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that it speaks of bones found already emptied, and רב זביד begins a different answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה adds רבי יוסי הגלילי and cites his ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that רבי יוסי הגלילי also holds that this kind of disqualified קרבן is burned immediately. He brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the פסוק about burning a חטאת as speaking only about פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה adds: רבי יוסי הגלילי also holds this view. It was taught in a ברייתא that רבי יוסי הגלילי says: the whole passage speaks only about the bulls and goats that are burned. It comes to teach that their disqualified ones are burned at the בית הבירה, and to make eating them a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds one more name to רבי יוחנן's list of תנאים who say a disqualified קרבן is burned right away. He sets up his proof by quoting a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא ו says that any חטאת whose blood was brought inside must be burned. Most people read it as speaking about a regular חטאת whose blood wrongly entered the היכל. רבי יוסי הגלילי says instead that it speaks only about the special inner חטאות, the פרים and שעירים הנשרפים. For those offerings, the פסוק teaches where to burn them if they become פסול and adds a prohibition against eating them.

keyTerms.meaning: the bulls whose blood is brought inside the היכל and whose bodies are burned
the goats whose blood is brought inside and whose bodies are burned
a place on the הר הבית where disqualified קדשים were burned

steps.confusionAlert: At this point you cannot yet see how this ברייתא connects to the case of the owners. The connection only shows up in the next two steps, when רבי יוסי הגלילי explains his source for a regular חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה מוֹסִיף, אַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
phrases.english: Rabba adds: even Rabbi Yosei HaGelili (holds this way).
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
The entire passage, all of it,
speaks only
about the bulls that are burned and the goats that are burned,
phrases.notes: The inner חטאות whose blood is brought inside the היכל.

phrases.english: to burn their disqualified ones at the place of the bira,
and to place a negative prohibition on eating them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מוֹסִיף, אַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from the previous daf of תנאים who say a disqualified פסח is burned immediately.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי is one of the תנאים who agree that such a קרבן is burned immediately. His ברייתא reads the פסוק as referring only to the inner חטאות.

steps.title: The חכמים ask for the source for a regular חטאת whose blood went inside
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי יוסי הגלילי: if the פסוק is only about the inner חטאות, where do we learn that a regular חטאת whose blood entered the היכל must be burned?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: a חטאת whose blood entered the innermost area, from where do we know it is burned?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים point out a gap that his reading creates. They ask him for a different source for the regular case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a regular חטאת whose blood was wrongly brought inside must be burned. Since רבי יוסי הגלילי used up the usual פסוק for the inner חטאות, he now needs another פסוק for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: the innermost area (here, inside the היכל)

phrases.english: They said to him: a sin-offering whose blood entered
into the innermost area, from where (do we know it is burned)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּכְנַס דָּמָהּ לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the result of רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What פסוק teaches that a regular חטאת whose blood entered the היכל is burned?

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from the פסוק 'Behold, its blood was not brought inside'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי answers from ויקרא י. משה said 'its blood was not brought inside', which implies that if it had gone out, or if its blood had gone in, it would be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Behold, its blood was not brought into the holy place within.' This implies that if it went out, or if its blood went in, it is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי gives a different פסוק as the source. This answer is what shows רבה that he agrees with burning immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's words put two cases side by side: the meat going out, and the blood coming in. A חטאת whose meat went out (יוצא) is burned immediately, so a חטאת whose blood came in is also burned immediately. So רבי יוסי הגלילי burns a קרבן right away even when its meat is fine and only the blood had a problem. רבה compares this to the case where only the owners had a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: behold, its blood was not brought (ויקרא י:יח)
by inference; it is implied that

steps.whyThisMatters: This derivation puts 'blood entered' in the same group as 'meat went out', which is burned immediately. That is the basis for רבה adding רבי יוסי הגלילי to the list.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: ״הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ
phrases.english: He said to them: 'Behold, its blood was not brought'
'into the holy place within,'
which implies that if it (the meat) goes out,
or alternatively if its blood enters, it is (immediately) burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ פְּנִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ויקרא י:יח. The פסוק links 'blood entered' with 'meat went out', so both are burned immediately.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן did not include רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן left out רבי יוסי הגלילי for a reason. The blood and the meat are one unit, but the owners are a separate matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן holds: blood and meat are one matter. The owners are a different matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן did not count רבי יוסי הגלילי when he listed who agrees with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A problem in the blood counts as a problem in the קרבן itself, because blood and meat belong together. That is why it can be treated like יוצא and burned right away. When the owners become טמא or die, the animal itself is fine and only something outside it changed. So we cannot prove that רבי יוסי הגלילי would burn it immediately in that case.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה compares a problem in the blood to a problem with the owners. רבי יוחנן separates them: the blood is part of the קרבן itself, while the owners are outside it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan holds:
Blood and meat are one matter.
The owners are a different matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: דָּם וּבָשָׂר חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבה's addition in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A problem in the blood is like a problem with the owners. Both are problems outside the meat, so רבי יוסי הגלילי would agree in both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood is part of the קרבן itself, and the owners are outside it. So רבי יוסי הגלילי's view about blood does not prove what he holds about the owners.

steps.title: משנה: bones, sinews, and leftover meat are burned on the sixteenth
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that the bones, sinews, and נותר of the קרבן פסח are burned on the 16th of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The bones, the sinews, and the נותר are burned on the sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה about what to do with the parts of the פסח that were left over or could not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bones still have marrow, but they cannot be eaten because it is forbidden to break the bones of the פסח. The sinews are also not eaten. All of these, together with the leftover meat, must be burned. The burning is pushed to the 16th because the 15th is יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: sacrificial meat left past its time

phrases.english: MISHNA: The bones, the sinews, and the leftover meat
are burned on the sixteenth (of Nisan).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעֲצָמוֹת וְהַגִּידִין וְהַנּוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bones, sinews, and נותר of the פסח are burned on the 16th of ניסן.

steps.title: If the sixteenth is on שבת, burn on the seventeenth
steps.stepSummary: If the 16th falls on שבת, the burning waits until the 17th. Burning these parts does not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the sixteenth falls on שבת, they are burned on the seventeenth, because they do not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds what to do when the usual day is שבת, and gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה to burn leftover קדשים does not override שבת or יום טוב. So it waits for the first regular weekday. This same reason also explains the first rule: it is not done on the 15th because that day is יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: Burning נותר never overrides שבת or יום טוב. It is always done on the first weekday after the 15th.

phrases.english: If the sixteenth falls on Shabbat,
they are burned on the seventeenth,
because they do not override

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: neither Shabbat nor the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case where the 16th falls on שבת, and gives the reason behind the timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning נותר does not override שבת or יום טוב, so it waits until the 17th when the 16th is שבת.

steps.title: Bones that held leftover meat make hands impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב מרי בר אבוה quoting רבי יצחק: bones of קדשים that held נותר make the hands טמא, because they became a base for a forbidden thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב מרי בר אבוה said in the name of רבי יצחק: Bones of קדשים that held נותר make the hands impure, because they became a base for a forbidden thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא on our משנה begins with a new rule. Bones that held leftover sacrificial meat are treated like the leftover meat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נותר (meat left past its time) makes hands טמא by rabbinic law. רבי יצחק adds that the bones holding that meat get the same status. His reason is that anything serving as a base (בסיס) for a forbidden item is treated like that item.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat left over past the time allowed for eating it
They make the hands ritually impure (a rabbinic decree)
A base or holder for a forbidden item

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Mari bar Avuh said
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Bones of sacrifices that held leftover meat
phrases.notes: The leftover meat was on them or inside them (the marrow) after the eating time ended.

phrases.english: make the hands impure,
since they became a base for a forbidden thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 5 with a related rule about bones of קדשים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bones that held נותר make hands טמא, because they served as a base for a forbidden item.

steps.title: Suggesting support from the משנה about burning bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה, which says the bones, sinews, and נותר of the פסח are burned on the 16th, supports רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this supports him: 'The bones, the sinews, and the נותר are burned on the sixteenth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a proof for רבי יצחק from our own משנה. This line only sets up the proof. The next steps explain how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the bones together with the נותר as things that must be burned. This hints that the bones have the same status as the נותר. The גמרא now has to show why that reading is forced.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
The bones, the sinews, and the leftover
are burned on the sixteenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה as possible support for רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's rule that שימוש נותר gives the bones the status of נותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה requiring the bones of the פסח to be burned with the נותר on the 16th.

steps.title: Which kind of bones is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of bones these are. If they have no marrow, there is no reason to burn them. They could just be thrown away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case of bones is this? If you say they have no marrow inside, why burn them? Let us just throw them away!
steps.whatsHappening: To build the proof, the גמרא pins down which bones the משנה means. It first rules out bones without marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only edible parts of a קרבן need burning when they become נותר. An empty bone is not food, so it would not need burning. So the משנה cannot be talking about empty bones.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: These bones, what is the case?
If you say there is no marrow in them,
why burn them? Let us throw them away!
phrases.notes: Something that is not edible does not need burning as נותר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי עֲצָמוֹת הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case in the משנה so the proof can work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the bones in the משנה are empty bones or bones with marrow.

steps.title: It must be bones with marrow inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה must be talking about bones that still have marrow in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that they have marrow in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. These are bones with marrow inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marrow is edible meat of the קרבן. Once the eating time passes, that marrow is real נותר. So the bones here are holding נותר, which is exactly רבי יצחק's case.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that they have marrow in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא, דְּאִית בְּהוּ מוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9: the bones contain marrow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about bones that contain marrow, which became נותר.

steps.title: Why burn the bones unless holding leftover matters?
steps.stepSummary: If שימוש נותר matters, the bones themselves need burning. If it does not matter, we could break the bones, burn only the marrow, and throw the bones away. So the משנה seems to prove that שימוש נותר matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say holding נותר is significant: that is why the bones need burning. But if holding נותר is nothing, why burn them? Let us break them, take out their marrow, burn the marrow, and throw away the bones! So we learn from this that holding נותר is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The משנה burns the whole bone, not just the marrow, and that only makes sense if the bone itself became like נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a simpler option: crack the bone, burn the marrow, and discard the bone. Since the משנה does not do that, it seems the bone itself needs burning. That fits רבי יצחק's view that the bone took on the status of the נותר it held.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
Serving as a holder for נותר

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that holding leftover meat is significant,
because of that they need burning.
But if you say
that holding leftover meat is nothing,
why do they need burning?
Let us break them and take out their marrow,
burn the marrow, and throw away the bones.
Rather, is it not so? Learn from this
that holding leftover meat is significant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא שִׁימּוּשׁ נוֹתָר מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case set up in step 10 to complete the proof begun in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's rule that שימוש נותר makes the bone like נותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה burns the whole bone instead of just extracting and burning the marrow.

steps.title: Rejected: the bones are burned because they may not be broken
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Holding נותר may really be nothing. The משנה burns the bones because the תנא holds that the איסור of breaking a bone of the פסח applies even to a פסול פסח, so the marrow cannot be taken out.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Really, I can tell you that holding נותר is nothing. But this תנא holds that 'in it' (do not break a bone in it) applies to a valid פסח, and even to a disqualified one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It gives a different reason why the bones must be burned whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed we could simply crack the bones and take out the marrow. But the Torah says 'do not break a bone in it' about the פסח, and this תנא applies that איסור even to a פסח that is now פסול. Since the bones cannot be broken, the only way to burn the marrow is to burn the whole bone, so the משנה tells us nothing about שימוש נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In it', from 'וְעֶצֶם לֹא תִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ' (do not break a bone in it), שמות יב:מו
Disqualified, no longer fit to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא decided that holding נותר is nothing. It only showed that this משנה does not prove anything either way, because there is another reason to burn the bones.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempted proof for רבי יצחק fails. The bones of the פסח are burned whole because breaking them is forbidden even when the פסח is פסול, not necessarily because they held נותר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the איסור of breaking a bone of the פסח can reach even a פסח that may no longer be eaten. That changes how its leftovers must be handled.

phrases.english: They say: No,
really, I can tell you
that holding leftover meat is nothing,
and he (the tanna) holds: 'in it' applies to a valid one,
phrases.notes: Refers to the איסור of breaking a bone of the פסח.

phrases.english: and even to a disqualified one.
phrases.notes: So the bones cannot be broken to remove the marrow, and they must be burned whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 11 by giving another reason the bones must be burned.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not reject רבי יצחק's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the bones could be broken to remove the marrow. But breaking a bone of the פסח is forbidden even when it is פסול.

steps.title: Can the bone-breaking ban really apply to a disqualified פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 12. A משנה teaches that someone who breaks a bone of a טמא פסח does not get מלקות, so the ban should not apply to a פסול פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think the ban applies even to a disqualified פסח? Didn't we learn: 'But one who leaves over meat of a pure פסח, or breaks a bone of an impure פסח, does not get forty lashes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in Step 12. It quotes a משנה that seems to say breaking a bone of a disqualified פסח is not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said our משנה burns the bones because breaking a bone is forbidden even in a פסול פסח. But another משנה says that one who breaks a bone of a טמא פסח gets no מלקות. A טמא פסח is a פסול פסח, so the ban seems to apply only to a valid one.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (Can you really think so?)
But didn't we learn in a משנה
One who leaves meat over past its time

phrases.english: Even with a disqualified one — can that enter your mind?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back on the answer from Step 12.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
But one who leaves over meat of a pure Pesach
and one who breaks a bone of an impure Pesach
phrases.notes: This is the part that creates the difficulty.

phrases.english: does not receive the forty lashes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ בְּפָסוּל סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise that Step 12 used to reject the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 12 that the איסור of שבירת עצם applies even to a פסול פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says there is no מלקות for breaking a bone of a טמא (פסול) פסח. So the ban does not apply to a פסול פסח.

steps.title: Answer: a פסח that was once valid is different from one that never was
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Our משנה is talking about a פסח that was valid at some point and only later became נותר. The other משנה is talking about a טמא פסח that was never valid at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it had a time when it was valid. There, it never had a time when it was valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that the two משניות are talking about two different kinds of disqualified פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that became נותר was valid before it was left over, so the ban on breaking a bone already applied to it and still stays. The טמא פסח in the other משנה was impure from the start and was never valid, so the ban never applied. Step 12's defense stands, but only for a פסח that had a valid moment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
A time when it was valid or fit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer says a טמא פסח is not disqualified. Both cases are פסול. The only difference is whether the קרבן was ever valid before it became פסול.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
here — where it had a time when it was valid,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה: meat that became נותר was valid before it was left over.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: there — where it did not have a time when it was valid.
phrases.notes: This is the other משנה: a טמא פסח that was never valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא): the two משניות are talking about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every פסול פסח is the same, so the ban either applies to all of them or to none.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies to a פסח that had שעת הכושר and then became פסול. It does not apply to one that was never valid.

steps.title: Which תנא makes this distinction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that it matters whether the קרבן was ever valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who makes a distinction between a קרבן that had a time when it was valid and one that did not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the distinction it just made. This sets up the next step, which names the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer based on a distinction is stronger when we can show that a real תנא holds it. The גמרא wants to anchor Step 14 in a known opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Who makes a distinction for himself

phrases.english: And who is the Tanna who distinguishes
between one that had a time when it was valid
and one that did not have a time when it was valid?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תַּנָּא דְּשָׁנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the distinction used in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds the שעת הכושר distinction.

steps.title: It is רבי יעקב, as a ברייתא shows
steps.stepSummary: The distinction belongs to רבי יעקב. A ברייתא brings three views: the תנא קמא (only a valid פסח), רבי יעקב (once valid, then disqualified, still counts), and רבי שמעון (no disqualified פסח counts).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יעקב, as it was taught: 'And you shall not break a bone in it.' 'In it' means a valid one and not a disqualified one. רבי יעקב says: if it had a time when it was valid and then became disqualified, the ban on breaking a bone applies. If it never had a time when it was valid, the ban does not apply. רבי שמעון says: in both cases, the ban does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the distinction is רבי יעקב's opinion. It quotes a ברייתא that shows his view next to two other views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בו' in the פסוק limits the ban to a כשר פסח. רבי יעקב reads it so that a פסח which was once valid stays included even after it becomes פסול. That matches both משניות as explained in Step 14. רבי שמעון disagrees and frees every פסול פסח from the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
'And you shall not break a bone in it' (שמות יב:מו)
Breaking a bone (of the קרבן פסח)
Both this case and that case

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that our משנה (and the defense in Step 12) follows רבי יעקב. According to רבי שמעון, the defense would not work.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Ya'akov.
As it was taught in a Baraita:
"And you shall not break a bone in it,"
"in it" — in a valid one and not in a disqualified one.
phrases.notes: The view of the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov says:
if it had a time when it was valid and then became disqualified —
the prohibition of breaking a bone applies to it,
if it did not have a time when it was valid —
the prohibition of breaking a bone does not apply to it.
Rabbi Shimon says:
both this and that —
the prohibition of breaking a bone does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by naming the תנא and quoting his source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יעקב, who holds that a קרבן which had שעת הכושר and later became פסול is still under the ban on breaking a bone.

steps.title: A ברייתא: only פסח bones need burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as an objection. It says bones of other קדשים do not need burning, and only פסח bones do, because leaving them around could lead to a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: No bones of קדשים need burning, except bones of the פסח, because of the risk of a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an objection by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the source; the next steps explain how it attacks the idea that שימוש נותר matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats other קדשים bones differently from פסח bones. The only reason it gives for burning פסח bones is תקלה, the worry that someone may break them later. The גמרא will now examine what kind of bones these are.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
A mishap; a risk of sinning (here, breaking the bones later)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
All bones of sacrifices
do not require burning,
except for the bones of the Pesach
because of the risk of a mishap.
phrases.notes: Someone might come to break them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: כׇּל עַצְמוֹת הַקֳּדָשִׁים אֵין טְעוּנִין שְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, now against the view that שימוש נותר is significant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שימוש נותר מילתא היא (holding leftover meat matters).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא says other קדשים bones need no burning. The attack is completed in Step 19.

steps.title: What kind of bones is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. If the bones have no marrow, why would פסח bones need burning at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case with these bones? If you say they have no marrow, why do they need burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of bones the ברייתא means. It first rules out bones without marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Empty bones hold no נותר, so there is no reason to burn even פסח bones. So the ברייתא must be talking about bones that still have marrow. This is the same move as Steps 9-10, now applied to the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (How do we picture it?)

phrases.english: These bones — what is the case?
If you say there is no marrow in them,
why do they need burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי עֲצָמוֹת הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case in the ברייתא from Step 17 so the objection can be built.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the bones in the ברייתא have marrow in them or not.

steps.title: If holding נותר matters, other קדשים bones should need burning too
steps.stepSummary: The bones must have marrow. If שימוש נותר mattered, then other קדשים bones with marrow should also need burning. Yet the ברייתא says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious they have marrow. And if you think that holding נותר is significant, why don't bones of other קדשים need burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the objection. Bones with marrow hold נותר, so if that mattered, all קדשים bones would need burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marrow left in the bones becomes נותר. If a bone that holds נותר must be burned, then bones of every קרבן would need burning. The ברייתא says only פסח bones are burned, so it seems that שימוש נותר is not significant.

keyTerms.meaning: Serving as a holder for leftover sacrificial meat

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that there is marrow in them,
and if it enters your mind
that holding Notar is significant —
bones of other sacrifices —
why do they not require burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ שִׁימּוּשׁ נוֹתָר מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion that the bones have marrow to complete the objection begun in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שימוש נותר is significant.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bones with marrow hold נותר. If that required burning, all קדשים bones would need burning. The ברייתא says only פסח bones do, so holding נותר does not matter.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the ברייתא is about bones found with the marrow already removed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ברייתא is about bones found already emptied. With other קדשים, where breaking bones is allowed, we assume the marrow was taken out before it became נותר. So those bones never held נותר and need no burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What case are we dealing with here? Where one found them with the marrow removed. Bones of other קדשים, where the ban on breaking a bone does not apply, we assume the marrow was taken out before it became נותר. So they never held נותר and do not need burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the objection. He limits the ברייתא to a special case: bones found already emptied of marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other קדשים bones may be broken, so we assume the marrow was removed in time, before the meat became נותר. Those bones never held נותר, which is why they need no burning, and שימוש נותר can still matter. A פסח bone may not be broken, so its marrow could only have come out after it was already נותר, which is why it still needs burning.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a limited case)
He removed it (took the marrow out)

steps.whatToRemember: This answer works on רבי שמעון's view (step 16) that once a פסח is פסול, the ban on breaking its bones no longer applies. The ברייתא saying only פסח bones are burned does not disprove שימוש נותר. It is about emptied bones: other קדשים bones were emptied in time, but פסח bones could not be.
steps.confusionAlert: The bones in רב נחמן בר יצחק's case are now empty. The question is when the marrow came out. For other קדשים it came out before the time ran out. For a פסח it could not, because breaking its bones is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where one found them with the marrow removed:
bones of other sacrifices,
to which the prohibition of breaking a bone does not apply —
we assume he removed the marrow before they became Notar,
so they never served as a holder of Notar,
and they do not require burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Steps 17-19 by limiting the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limits the ברייתא to bones found already emptied of marrow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about bones full of marrow, so it proves that holding נותר does not require burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about emptied bones. Other קדשים bones were emptied before they became נותר, so they never held נותר. This leaves room for שימוש נותר to be significant.

steps.title: Why פסח bones held leftover marrow and need burning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק finishes his answer. With the פסח, breaking bones is forbidden. So the bones were emptied only after the meat became נותר. That makes them a holder of נותר (שימוש נותר), and they need burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the bones of the פסח are under the prohibition of breaking a bone. So it was only after they became נותר that someone emptied them. That means they held נותר, and they need burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer. It explains the other side of the contrast: why פסח bones, unlike other קדשים bones, do need burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other קדשים, the bones may be broken, so we assume the marrow was taken out while the meat was still allowed. A פסח bone may not be broken while the offering is valid, so the marrow was still inside when the meat became נותר, and it was removed only afterward, following רבי שמעון's view (step 16) that a disqualified פסח is no longer under the ban. Because these bones held נותר marrow, they count as שימוש נותר and must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking a bone, which is forbidden with a קרבן פסח
After they became leftover (past the time for eating)
He emptied them (took the marrow out)
Something that held or served leftover sacrificial meat
Burning, the required way to dispose of נותר

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, the difference is about timing. Other קדשים bones were emptied in time, before the meat became נותר. פסח bones could only be emptied after the meat became נותר, so they held נותר and need burning.
steps.confusionAlert: The bones themselves are not the problem. The issue is that the marrow inside them became נותר while it was still in the bone. That is what turns the bone into a 'holder' of נותר.

phrases.english: The bones of the Paschal offering,
which are subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone —
phrases.notes: So no one would break them while the פסח was still valid.

phrases.english: after they became leftover
phrases.notes: This follows רבי שמעון in the ברייתא of step 16: once the meat is פסול, like נותר, the bone ban is gone. רבי יעקב says a once-valid פסח stays under the ban.

phrases.english: is when one emptied them,
and so they became a holder of leftover,
and they require burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַצְמוֹת הַפֶּסַח, דְּיֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer from step 20 by contrasting פסח bones with other קדשים bones.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about bones found already emptied, and the deciding factor is when the emptying must have happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If שימוש נותר is the reason, then all קדשים bones with marrow should need burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only פסח bones needed burning. Since they could not be broken while the פסח was valid, they must have been emptied after the meat became נותר.

steps.title: רב זביד begins a different answer
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד offers another way to answer the objection from steps 17-19. He starts by defining a different case ('what are we dealing with here? such as...'). The details continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: What case are we dealing with here? A case such as...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different answer to the same objection, in the name of רב זביד. This line is only the setup. His actual case comes right after, on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase הכא במאי עסקינן tells us רב זביד will explain the ברייתא as talking about a specific case. He does not accept רב נחמן בר יצחק's 'already emptied bones' explanation as the only answer. He will offer his own way to explain why פסח bones are different.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a different answer here
'What case are we dealing with here?' — the opening of a case-narrowing answer

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
With what are we dealing here?
A case such as
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same objection that רב נחמן בר יצחק just answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing (אוקימתא), with details still to come
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to contradict the idea that שימוש נותר needs burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still pending: רב זביד's specific case appears on the next amud.
